card.name: Timing words in dosing instructions
card.fires_on: Small words and timing terms in dosing directions where a time of day or schedule relative to another event (bedtime, dialysis, meals, other drugs) is about to be named.

modes.label: Linking word before a time
modes.description: A word like 'at' or 'of' that leads into a time-of-day or timing phrase.
modes.example: the drug may be given in a single dose (not to exceed 300 mg)<< at>> bedtime.

modes.label: Spacing from other drugs
modes.description: Verbs like administer, or words in interaction notes, before 'at least X hours' separation.
modes.example: Intervention: In patients taking a bile acid sequestrant,<< administer>> pravastatin sodium at least

modes.label: Timing and level terms
modes.description: Words about timing or drug levels between doses, such as timing, day, trough.
modes.example: can be administered without regard to the<< timing>> of dialysis

card.writes: It pushes toward time-of-day and recurring-time words such as evening, morning and 'every time'.
card.plain: It lights up where a dosing instruction is about to say when in the day, or relative to something else, the drug is taken.
